answer.rationale: The write-path latency climb began roughly at the time of the release 2 hours ago, making the new build the leading suspect; memory_b1 records that rolling back a release cleared a prior checkout error spike without customer impact, and memory_b6 shows releases here are gated, so a known-stable prior build likely exists. Rollback preserves customer writes (no traffic shedding, unlike circuit breakers or failover risk) and is reversible. Peak settlement load is a confounder, so I am verifying b1 and b3 (capacity precedent) before committing; if verification shows b1's incident was error-rate-driven rather than latency-driven, add_capacity becomes the fallback.
